commit_message:
Bug 1855142 - Ensure IndexedDabaseManager::mLocale separately; r=dom-storage-reviewers,jari

mLocale is currently initialized in IndexedDatabaseManager::Init which is
called from IndexedDatabaseManager::GetOrCreate if the manager doesn't exist.
This can be a problem when IndexedDatabaseManager::GetOrCreate is called very
early,for example in nsLayoutStatics::Initialize in the parent process.

This is a preparation for moving IndexedDatabaseManager::GetOrCreate from
FactoryOp::Open to InitializeQuotaManager.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D189891

findings.title: Data race on mLocale string member without synchronization
findings.message: The EnsureLocale() function modifies mLocale member variable from the main thread without proper synchronization, while GetLocale() reads mLocale concurrently from worker threads. This creates a data race condition: the main thread can call EnsureLocale() multiple times (through IDBFactory::AllowedForWindowInternal, WorkerPrivate::GetLoadInfo, or RemoteWorkerChild::ExecWorkerOnMainThread), potentially reallocating the string buffer while DOM worker threads are reading it via GetLocale() called in IDBFactory::OpenInternal. This can lead to use-after-free or buffer overflow when the worker thread reads memory that has been freed or reallocated by the main thread.
findings.suggestion: Add a guard to prevent re-initialization of mLocale after it's been set. Introduce a boolean flag mLocaleInitialized and check it at the beginning of EnsureLocale() to return early if already initialized. Mark the flag with MOZ_GUARDED_BY for thread safety annotation.

findings.title: Unsafe concurrent access to mLocale from multiple call sites
findings.message: EnsureLocale() is called from multiple locations without coordination: IDBFactory::AllowedForWindowInternal (main thread), WorkerPrivate::GetLoadInfo (main thread), and RemoteWorkerChild::ExecWorkerOnMainThread (main thread). While all these callers run on the main thread, DOM worker threads concurrently access GetLocale() which reads mLocale. The lack of synchronization between the writing main thread and reading worker threads creates a TOCTOU-style race where mLocale can be modified between the worker thread's check and use.
findings.suggestion: Ensure EnsureLocale() is idempotent by only initializing mLocale once. Once initialized, subsequent calls should be no-ops. This prevents the string buffer from being reallocated while worker threads may be reading it.

ground_truth.root_cause: The EnsureLocale() function was introduced without synchronization or idempotency protection. It can be called multiple times from different code paths (IDBFactory::AllowedForWindowInternal, WorkerPrivate::GetLoadInfo, RemoteWorkerChild::ExecWorkerOnMainThread), and each call modifies the shared mLocale member. Meanwhile, DOM worker threads read this member via GetLocale() without any synchronization, creating a classic writer-reader race condition.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable write operation that modifies mLocale string without synchronization. Multiple calls can reallocate the string buffer (lines 648-650, 654-655) while worker threads are reading it, causing use-after-free or buffer overflow.

Contains the unsynchronized read operation on mLocale that runs on worker threads (called from IDBFactory::OpenInternal). This read can occur concurrently with EnsureLocale() writes from the main thread, creating a data race.

Calls GetLocale() from worker threads (line 664) to read mLocale while main thread may be modifying it. This is the primary reader call site that executes on DOM worker threads and triggers the race condition.

Calls EnsureLocale() from main thread (line 297) which can modify mLocale while worker threads are reading it via GetLocale(). One of multiple main-thread call sites that can trigger reallocation during concurrent reads.

Calls EnsureLocale() from main thread (line 2809) during worker initialization, which can modify mLocale string while other worker threads are concurrently reading it via GetLocale(), creating the write-read race.

Calls EnsureLocale() from main thread (line 237) during remote worker execution, potentially modifying mLocale while concurrent worker threads read it. This is a third main-thread write path that demonstrates the bug is not idempotent.
